scope: One immutable v2 route per database. Existing v1 retains all records; no implicit migration or reset.

storage.metadata: Exact built-in schema, profile/context/key check/receiver authority namespace, uint64 high H and retired floor F_R as fixed 8-byte big-endian BLOBs, prefix root, observed clock and encrypted latest retirement offer.
storage.live: Exactly the contiguous interval F_R+1..H, at most public W rows. Each row retains canonical final fact and full signed envelope/control evidence under distinct AEAD purposes bound to context, seq and derived ID.
storage.last_offer: One latest authenticated sender offer binds the current nonzero floor and root. Full retired history is intentionally absent; audit trusts authority transition integrity and sender signing policy.
storage.physical_limit: 16 MiB canonical image cap. Conservative per-route M+W*L admission now runs before database connection/creation and authority calls; see retention_capacity_contract.json. This bounds current canonical image only, not physical or total storage.

first_event: Verify pinned transport peer and receiver signer; dispatch unverified outer payload only to exact authenticated domain/schema parsers before state access.
BEGIN IMMEDIATE; require current authority image, enforce monotonic clock; reject seq<=floor and non-next unseen sequence; reject full window.
Reconstruct ACCEPTED from complete signed result within original expiry, or CLOSED from signed terminal control at/after expiry. Persist encrypted fact/evidence and high-water together.
Existing result replay must match exact stored envelope; terminal replies must match original descriptor and fact. First time/outcome never change. CLOSED rejects later results.
Audit next image; authority CAS accepts before local commit; only then return signed challenge/request-bound receipt.
retirement: Require sender-signed offer generated after durable sender confirmation. Signature alone is not an externally verifiable persistence proof.

Current authority fence and write lock; verify base floor/root, exact consecutive prefix and target root; DELETE prefix and advance floor/root/latest offer in one authoritative state transition, retaining H and clock.
Already applied target can return current checkpoint; smaller old targets cause no mutation and do not validate or reconstruct forgotten historical roots.
Old result or FINAL request is rejected; explicit RETIRED query returns current checkpoint, never invented outcome/time. Sender reconciles checkpoint against retained full archive.
clock: Business Rejected rolls back the business savepoint while committing observed clock through authority/local commit. Authentication failures precede state access. Infrastructure or image-cap failures can roll back the entire transaction; clock persistence is not claimed in those cases.
recovery: Explicit create/restore only. Missing local database cannot initialize itself. Stale image is fenced; restore exact current authority image under trusted schema, audit full facts and latest offer before commit and recheck authority head. No refund or new first event.
transport: Reuses RecipientTLSService and DeliverySender.exchange framing over loopback mTLS, with v2 signed payload dispatch. The peer fingerprint is provided by authenticated transport. This is an integration fixture, not a production deployment/management API or complete public observation protocol.
trust: Receiver and sender services/signers trusted; each authority linearizable and nonrollback. Separate files, namespaces, services and signing keys on one host do not establish independent production fault domains.

validation.crash_scope: Reference authority process exits only. Separate loopback mTLS fixture exercises lost result/retirement replies, not the full TLS crash matrix.
validation.mixed_fixture: Actual signed encrypted shared-account B4 N3 histogram (32 bytes) and count (8 bytes), sender L3/outbox, actual receiver facts, sender confirmation and retirement checkpoint.
coverage: window full then prefix retirement permits next record
accept/close race and both deterministic orders
lost acceptance and retirement replies preserve original fact
old local snapshot after retirement cannot resurrect rows
corrupt authority image rejected before restore commit
same identity with different signed evidence rejected
validation.negative_control: Rolling back both recipient and reference authority restores an old history and permits a different first-event time; local audit alone cannot detect joint authority rollback.

remaining: Scalable authority/history storage and bounded aggregate resources; current per-route image admission implemented
Production audit access, scalable archive retrieval, availability and retention governance
Independent COSE/CDDL interoperability and parser review
Cross-host authority fault tests, identity/key lifecycle and production nonrollback evidence
Complete P2 workflow, strong baselines and full public-observation refinement; broader P3-P6 goals
